sections.p03.s0: Read in order: environments and lockfiles, then pyproject.toml and layout, then entry points, then lint, type-check and release habits. Allow about two days, and try each idea in a throwaway project as you read, because the build section applies all of it to a real tool.
sections.p03.s1: Choose one earlier tool and do the steps in order; each depends on the one before. Budget about a week: a day for the restructure and pyproject.toml, a day for tooling, and the rest on fixtures, property tests and the README. Finish by installing from a clean venv.

p03.s0.0.how: Create a venv with python -m venv .venv, activate it, and compare sys.prefix and pip list inside and outside it. Install two packages, delete the folder, and rebuild it from a requirements.txt. Run where python to see which interpreter your shell finds.
p03.s0.0.done: You can explain what activation changes (PATH) and why two projects needing different versions of one library cannot share a global install.

p03.s0.1.how: Start a project with uv init, add two dependencies with uv add, and open uv.lock to see exact versions and hashes for every transitive dependency. Delete .venv, run uv sync and confirm the same versions come back.
p03.s0.1.done: You can explain the difference between a version range in pyproject.toml and a pin in the lockfile.

p03.s0.2.how: Write a pyproject.toml by hand with [build-system], [project] (name, version, requires-python, dependencies), a dev extra under [project.optional-dependencies] and a [tool.ruff] table. Install it with pip install -e . and check pip show.
p03.s0.2.done: The project installs in editable mode and you can say which table the build backend, the installer and Ruff each read.

p03.s0.3.how: Make a flat-layout package and run its tests from the project root: they pass without installing. Move it under src/ and watch the tests fail until you install it. That failure is the point: tests now run against the installed package, not the working directory.
p03.s0.3.done: You can explain how the current directory on sys.path hides files missing from the built wheel in a flat layout.

p03.s0.4.how: Add [project.scripts] with your-tool = "your_package.cli:main", reinstall, and run your-tool --help from another directory. Find the generated launcher in .venv/Scripts (Windows) or .venv/bin.
p03.s0.4.done: your-tool runs from any directory while the venv is active, and you can name the function it calls.

p03.s0.5.how: Install pre-commit, write a .pre-commit-config.yaml using the ruff-pre-commit hooks for ruff check --fix and ruff format, run pre-commit install, then commit a badly formatted file and watch the hook stop the commit.
p03.s0.5.done: A commit containing a lint error is rejected locally without you running any check by hand.

p03.s0.6.how: Write a GitHub Actions workflow that installs the project and runs mypy on every push and pull request. Push a commit with a deliberate type error, confirm the run fails, then fix it.
p03.s0.6.done: A pushed type error turns the CI run red, and the fix turns it green.

p03.s0.7.how: Read the SemVer spec and Keep a Changelog. Decide the version bump for three changes: a bug fix, a new option, a removed flag. Start a CHANGELOG.md with an Unreleased section and Added, Changed, Fixed and Removed headings.
p03.s0.7.done: You can say whether a change needs a major, minor or patch bump, and what a 0.x version does and does not promise.

p03.s1.0.how: Move the code into src/your_package/ with an __init__.py, put tests in tests/ beside src/, and change every import to use the package name. Install with pip install -e . and run pytest from the project root.
p03.s1.0.done: pytest passes after installation, and import your_package works from any other directory.

p03.s1.1.how: Fill in name, version, description, readme, requires-python, license, dependencies, a dev extra and [project.scripts]. Build with python -m build or uv build, install the wheel into a fresh venv, and run the command there.
p03.s1.1.done: The wheel installs into a clean venv and the CLI command runs there with no source checkout on the path.

p03.s1.2.how: Add [tool.ruff] with line-length and target-version, [tool.ruff.lint] with a select list (start with E, F, I, B, UP), and [tool.mypy] with strict = true or a stated subset. Run both and fix or explicitly ignore every finding.
p03.s1.2.done: ruff check ., ruff format --check . and mypy all exit 0 using settings from pyproject.toml only.

p03.s1.3.how: Find setup repeated across test files (sample config, fake data, temp folders) and move it into fixtures in tests/conftest.py. Use the built-in tmp_path for files and choose each fixture's scope on purpose. Run pytest --fixtures to list them.
p03.s1.3.done: No test file carries its own copy of shared setup, and pytest --fixtures lists yours with docstrings.

p03.s1.4.how: Pick a function with a clear invariant, such as a round trip (parse(format(x)) == x) or output that is always sorted. Write a @given test using hypothesis.strategies, run it, and read the shrunk example if it fails.
p03.s1.4.done: The property test runs in your normal pytest run and you can state its invariant in one sentence.

p03.s1.5.how: Write four sections: install (exact commands from a clean machine), usage (real command lines and their output), configuration (every option and its default), limitations (what the tool does not handle). Then follow the README word for word in a new venv.
p03.s1.5.done: Someone following only the README in a fresh environment can install, configure and run the tool.
